items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S3183

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act authorizing the city of Middletown, county of Orange, to enter
into a contract and sell some or all of its delinquent tax liens held
by such city to a private party; and providing for the repeal of such
provisions upon expiration thereof


 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :
This bill provides, for two years, the authority for the City of
Middletown to sell tax liens to a private collection entity.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :
Section 1 - City of Middletown shall have the right to enter into a
contract to sell some or all of its delinquent tax liens to a private
patty subject to:

* Consideration to be paid shall be more or less than the face amount
of the liens sold.

* City of Middletown shall set the terms and conditions of the
contract of sale.

* City of Middletown shall provide property owners with at least 30
days advance notice.

* The sale of a tax lien shall not operate to shorten the otherwise
applicable redemption period or change the applicable interest rate.

*Upon expiration of the redemption period the lien may be foreclosed
as provided in section 1194 of the Real Property Tax Law. The
procedure shall be the procedure prescribed by article 13 of the real
property actions and proceedings law.

* The provisions of title 5 of article 11 of real property tax law
shall apply, as far as is practicable, to a contract for the sale of
the tax liens.

 EFFECTS OF PRESENT LAW WHICH THIS BILL WOULD ALTER :
Municipalities must request enacting legislation to enable the sale of
delinquent tax liens to private patties.

 JUSTIFICATION :
The bill was requested by the City of Middletown. The city has
attempted to collect these liens on its own but it imposes an
unreasonable financial burden on city taxpayers.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
New in 2009.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately and shall expire and be deemed
repealed on December 31, 2012.

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S3183A

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to authorize the city of Middletown to enter into a contract to
sell some or all of the delinquent tax liens held by such city to a
private party; and providing for the repeal of such provisions upon
expiration thereof


 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :
To expand the options available to the City of Middletown to
efficiently and effectively manage the collection of delinquent
property taxes.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :
Permits the City of Middletown, under enumerated circumstances, to
enter into a contract to sell some or all of their delinquent tax
liens to a private party. The contract must be entered into by
December 31, 2009, and this authority sunsets on December 31, 2011.
Provides "consumer protections" for affected property owners,
including a requirement for thirty days notification, assurance that
the existing redemption periods and interest rates remain unchanged,
and imposition of the procedural requirements relating to foreclosure
of a mortgage or tax lien sale by the Municipal Bond Bank Agency.

 EXISTING LAW :
Municipalities must request enacting legislation to enable the sale of
delinquent tax liens to private parties.

 JUSTIFICATION :
This bill was introduced at the request of the City of Middletown,
Orange County. This legislation will continue to provide Middletown
with the same option which has been utilized by the other cities of
Schenectady and Amsterdam in previous legislation.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
This is a new bill for 2009.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
None to the State.

 LOCAL FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
Should improve the fiscal status of the City of Middletown through an
infusion of cash upon the sale of delinquent tax liens.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
Immediate, and expires on December 31, 2011.

summary: Authorizes the city of Middletown to sell its delinquent tax liens to a private party.
